sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Players on Steam so far seem delighted with Modern Warfare 4's campaign, making it one of the most well-received Call of Dutys in recent history
sources.text: It may be hard to believe, given all the Call of Duty: Modern 4 pre-launch community drama and the beta's lower-than-expected numbers on PC , but the final game may have turned things around - so far, at least. On Steam, Infinity Ward 's final chapter in the Modern Warfare sub-series currently has a Very Positive (92 percent) rating based on over 3,100 user reviews . Modern Warfare 4's campaign early access went live Friday, and the review rating has been improving steadily as players have experienced more of the campaign's missions. Many have likely finished it by now; the campaign is a little over six-hours in length, after all. Gaining access to the campaign on Friday required pre-ordering any of the game's editions digitally. Modern Warfare 4's official release isn't until 23rd October, which makes it hard to determine the current number of players, because SteamDB , our source for this data, can't reveal numbers without its tracking bot having a copy of the game. Setting aside player numbers, the sentiment around Modern Warfare 4 is considerably more positive at the outset compared to last year's Black Ops 7, currently sitting at Mostly Negative (37 percent) . While review ratings change over time with each major update, Modern Warfare 4 is currently the highest-rated Call of Duty in over a decade. However, it's worth bearing in mind that the people playing the game are likely the series' most keen players, so perhaps they're more lenient towards it. We haven't had a chance to review the game yet, having only received code late last week, but IGN published a COD: Modern Warfare 4 campaign review on Friday, scoring it 8/10. In the rebooted Modern Warfare series, the 2019 Modern Warfare game comes closest in average player sentiment with a Mostly Positive rating (79 percent) . 2022's Modern Warfare 2 is far lower with a Mixed rating (45 percent) . Outside of Infinity Ward's output, Black Ops: Cold War is close at Mostly Positive (79 percent) . Modern Warfare 4's next big moment is the anticipated release of DMZ, the game's extraction shooter mode. Like the campaign, DMZ is available early for pre-orders, unlocking tomorrow, 20th October . Finally, on 23rd October, traditional multiplayer becomes available, which is when we're likely to see a shift in user sentiment, if one is going to happen.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Modern Warfare 4 campaign launches to 94% positive Steam reviews, way ahead of Black Ops 7
sources.text: The campaign for Call of Duty : Modern Warfare 4 is now available for those who pre-ordered, and PC players in particular seem pretty taken by it. The single-player mode has debuted to a strong rating on Steam, indicating this particular installment could be a big one for the franchise. Although Modern Warfare 4 isn't fully out until this coming Friday, October 23, pre-orders come with early access to the campaign. During the beta, this was relegated to a single mission, but now you can knock out the whole thing if you'd like. You'd think this would be a questionable move by Activision and Infinity Ward , but it might just be quite shrewd. If you go on the game's page on Steam, you can see the rating is currently riding extremely high. At time of writing, Modern Warfare 4 is sitting at Very Positive on Valve 's marketplace, based on 94% of reviews. That's a strong opening for any game, and it's especially good for Call of Duty. We don't have hard data on the first weeks of many individual entries of the long-running FPS, but this definitely outdoes the initial feedback on Black Ops 7 and Modern Warfare 3. You can see charts of their reviews going back to launch weeks, and neither were anywhere close to that amount. Whomever came up with the bold move to simply make the campaign part of the perks for being an early adopter, they were onto something. It helps that apparently Infinity Ward's made a good one, which includes 16 missions spread across several locations around the world. Call of Duty campaigns have tended to be a little forgettable over the last ten years or so, since the multiplayer modes and Warzone took prominence. As someone who loves a good solo FPS, it pleases me to see that Modern Warfare 4 is bucking the trend. You can pre-order now if any kind of FOMO is setting in. He previously served as Senior Anime Writer at Dexerto and News Editor at The Digital Fix, on top of providing work for Variety, IGN, Den of Geek, PC Gamer, and many more. Besides Studio Ghibli, horror movies, and The Muppets, he enjoys action-RPGs, heavy metal, and pro-wrestling. He interviewed Animal once, not that he won’t stop going on about it or anything. sources.title: Cyberpunk 2077 terá atualização gratuita com combate usando duas armas e conteúdo de Edgerunners 2
sources.text: A CD Projekt RED anunciou uma nova atualização gratuita para Cyberpunk 2077 . Chamada de Update 2.5 , a novidade será lançada em 22 de outubro de 2026 e incluirá conteúdos inspirados na segunda temporada de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners , que estreou nesta terça-feira (20) na Netflix. Entre as principais mudanças estão a possibilidade de utilizar duas armas simultaneamente durante os combates e novas opções de personalização dos implantes cibernéticos do protagonista. Inicialmente, a atualização estará disponível para PC, PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S . A versão para Nintendo Switch 2 também receberá o conteúdo, mas em uma data posterior, ainda não divulgada. Uma das principais novidades do patch será a introdução de um estilo de combate que permite utilizar duas armas ao mesmo tempo. A desenvolvedora ainda não detalhou quais categorias de armamentos serão compatíveis com a mecânica ou como ela funcionará durante as partidas. Outra mudança confirmada envolve os implantes cibernéticos, que receberão novas possibilidades de personalização. Entretanto, a CD Projekt RED não informou quais componentes poderão ser modificados nem se as novidades terão impacto direto nos atributos do personagem. A atualização também incluirá itens inspirados em Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 , ampliando a conexão entre o jogo e a animação. Para detalhar o conteúdo, a desenvolvedora realizará uma nova edição do REDstreams na quarta-feira, 21 de outubro, às 12h (horário de Brasília) . Durante a transmissão, a empresa apresentará as principais mudanças do Update 2.5 e divulgará a lista completa de novidades. A expectativa é que o evento esclareça o funcionamento do combate com duas armas, as opções de personalização e os conteúdos relacionados ao anime. A atualização acompanha a estreia de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 , segunda temporada da animação produzida em parceria com o estúdio japonês Trigger. Os dez episódios chegaram à Netflix em 20 de outubro de 2026. Diferentemente da primeira temporada, a nova produção apresenta uma história independente, com novos personagens envolvidos em uma trama de vingança e redenção em Night City. A direção é de Kai Ikarashi, e a narrativa acompanha personagens que tentam sobreviver aos conflitos da cidade. Ainda não foi divulgado quais elementos específicos da nova temporada estarão presentes em Cyberpunk 2077 . Com o lançamento do Update 2.5, a CD Projekt RED amplia o conteúdo do RPG enquanto aproveita a chegada da nova animação ao catálogo da Netflix. Rachele Victoria é formada em Letras, MBA em Inovação e atua há 10 anos com comunicação e conteúdo gamer. Amazon Prime também é feito para jogadores! Todo mês, obtenha itens exclusivos, jogos grátis, uma assinatura gratuita na Twitch.tv e muito mais com sua assinatura Prime . Clique aqui para um teste gratuito de 30 dias .

The announcement does mention âcyberware customizationâ and âa new dual-wielding playstyle.â as some of the additions in the 2.5 update. Based on the promo image, which shows protagonist V standing back to back with Weak Kingsley, one of the characters in Edgerunners II , there may also be some new photo mode poses and other features, as V is shown dual-wielding guns, which is not a pose typically seen in-game. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is getting a new DLC to hold people over until the next game, though, so the wait wonât feel that long. sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Is Getting a Big Update This Week
sources.text: It'll feature content inspired by Edgerunners 2 Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is out on Netflix: It's a standalone sequel to the first Edgerunners anime from 2022, and both seasons connect to CD Projekt Red's RPG Cyberpunk 2077 . To celebrate the release of the new anime, CDPR has announced Cyberpunk 2077 will receive a new update this week. CD Projekt Red is calling it the Edgerunners 2 Update or Update 2.5, and it will include "content inspired by the anime," according to a news release. Also on the way are "a range of other new items and features." That is all CD Projekt Red has shared at this time. The publisher will host a livestream on Wednesday at 11 a.m. EDT to go into detail about what the update entails. You can watch the stream on Twitch, YouTube, and Steam. Or ignore the stream and go into the new update blind. You do you. Edgerunners 2 Update will be released on Oct. 22 for PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X, while the update for the Nintendo Switch 2 version will "follow shortly." Like Cyberpunk 2077 , Cyberpunk: Edgerunners takes place in the futuristic Night City, where gang violence and body modification run rampant. Season 1 followed the rise and fall of David Martinez, undone by an excess of cybernetic implants. Season 2 follows a new cast trying to survive in the chaos of Night City. "With the intertwining stories of a veteran edgerunner, a young cinephile, a chrome-obsessed delinquent, and a Snake Nation netrunner, the series tells a raw and emotional tale of vengeance and redemption," the news release says. Polygon's Ryan Epps saw the first episode over the summer at Anime Expo and enjoyed it. "Packed with incredible colors, gorgeous framing, and punchy sound design, Edgerunners 2 is a fresh take on a beloved world," he wrote .

stories.title: Final Fantasy Resonance review: "A breezy nostalgia-laced JRPG that gives the HD-2D style a shot in the arm"
stories.summary: A defunct gacha mobile game is reborn into a classic but modern adventure

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Final Fantasy Resonance review: "A breezy nostalgia-laced JRPG that gives the HD-2D style a shot in the arm"
sources.text: Like Octopath Traveler 0, Final Fantasy Resonance is a rejuvenated way to experience a story once bound and lost to mobile. It may not reinvent the series, but in giving the HD-2D style a much needed upgrade this retro-modern refresh feels like a mainline adventure in its own right. Engaging battles that mix classic and modern Final Fantasy conventions Generous cadence of side quests and challenges CG sequences can jar with HD-2D presentation Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy. Final Fantasy Resonance is at once a nostalgia-laced antidote for the longtime fans who have felt alienated by the recent 3D iterations turning their backs on the series' turn-based traditions as well as Square Enix giving its trademarked HD-2D style a much needed shot in the arm. While I've been enamored by this retro-modern style since its introduction in 2018's Octopath Traveler , over time it's been losing its charm, as the same presentation had been wheeled out in successive nostalgic outings, though at least Dragon Quest 7 Reimagined had the good grace to try something different . Nonetheless, its legacy of pixel-based classics like Final Fantasy 6 meant it was only a matter of time before a Final Fantasy title would receive the HD-2D treatment while also finding ways for the aesthetic to feel fresh again. Ironically, it's done that not through a brand new game but with an adaptation of mobile spin-off Final Fantasy Brave Exvius. My first Final Fantasy was Final Fantasy 8, whereafter I have played through most of the series' mainline instalments, including the 2D classics, as well as its many spin-offs, although Final Fantasy: Brave Exvius had been a blind spot. Using a Nintendo Switch 2 code provided by the publisher, I spent about 40 hours playing through Final Fantasy Resonance, completing all discovered side quests before reaching the credits. – Reviewer Alan Wen Release date: October 22, 2026 Platform(s): PC, PS5, Xbox Series X, Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo Switch Developer: In-house, Lancarse Publisher: Square Enix Square Enix reworking its mobile catalog to console may not be new, as it has done successfully with Octopath Traveler 0 , and less so with Various Daylife , but Final Fantasy Resonance is more significant as it excavates a since discontinued mobile game. The work from Square Enix Creative Studio 5 and Lancarse is even more extensive than just an act of preservation or removing the gacha elements that had been why Brave Exvius passed me by when it was available . While its story and characters remain intact, the whole presentation and experience has been overhauled to feel like a very classic yet fresh Final Fantasy adventure that stands on its own two feet. Just about everything in Final Fantasy Resonance harks back to the series' classic hallmarks , from turn-based battles with a party size of four characters to the explorable overworld of Lapis peppered with towns, dungeons, random encounters, and – of course – a story that revolves around crystals. As a knight of the kingdom of Grandshelt, your protagonist Rain finds himself setting out on a journey to find the legendary crystals before each can be destroyed by a mysterious group of elite armored warriors calling themselves the Sworn Six. There's plenty that follows a largely conventional structure – visit a new region, discover a problem the locals are having where one of the characters end up joining your party, and a dungeon that culminates in a fight with one of the Sworn Six – but it's not really a criticism when the execution of this formula is done so well. Sure, there are some familiar characterizations, from a leading man obliviously caught in a love triangle, to a feisty mechanic who's often butting heads with the sleazeball of the group, but these are fun characters to spend time with. Even the game's villains are written with pathos, while the series' recurring Espers have their own personality as you fight for the right to summon them in battle. It's all bolstered by the presentation that's a substantial level-up from past HD-2D games. While Final Fantasy Resonance does make use of voice-acting as well as having dialogue text accompanied by expressive character illustrations – the latter introduced in this year's The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales – its biggest improvement comes from the spritework, which are bigger and feature more animations than what would have been feasible for a 16-bit Final Fantasy. Another subtle yet meaningful shift seen early on is how it's not presented with the same top-down medium-wide camera but actually leverages the fact that the game is made up of 3D environments. It's not that Final Fantasy Resonance strives to be cinematic, but a simple change of the camera to a close-up, more dynamic angles during a boss encounter, or one of your party member's show-stopping Limit Bursts, does a lot to make HD-2D feel fresh again. Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week It's only undermined by the occasional use of CG sequences when you're summoning Espers or Visions, the latter including manifestations of characters from the numbered Final Fantasy titles. Given how their CG sequences are taken straight from Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, I imagine they looked far more spectacular blowing up on your smartphone back in the day. I personally found these transitions at odds with the HD-2D style, and it's perhaps weirder if playing the game with English audio since the CG Visions are only voiced in Japanese. Visions are nonetheless a core component in Final Fantasy Resonance and are significantly overhauled from Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, where they were unlocked through a gacha system. This remake has just 26 from the hundreds of the mobile title but nixes any monetization

sources.name: Video Games Chronicle
sources.title: Final Fantasy Resonance Review: A nostalgic JRPG limited by its mobile origins
sources.text: Alongside Square Enix’s Pixel Remasters and other HD-2D games, Resonance isn’t an essential experience Final Fantasy Resonance doesnât really have to do anything new. This is a new adaptation of an older mobile game, Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, with the gacha system removed and progression completely reworked to befit a more standard, single-player, premium JRPG. Those are all points in its favor, and Resonance evokes the atmosphere and spirit of classic Final Fantasy, but itâs still an adaptation of that older mobile game. Resonance is set in a Final Fantasy world thatâs familiar, but not the same as the ones youâve played before (unless youâve literally played Brave Exvius). Armor-clad knights, elemental crystals, spirits, and summons. Everything about the setting, character designs, and major story beats feels cherry-picked from classic FF games that fans are nostalgic for. Thatâs not necessarily a bad thing. Final Fantasy games have a unique vibe that other long-running JRPG series just canât quite muster, and Resonance manages to evoke that atmosphere even when some numbered entries struggle to do so. On the other hand, this familiarity makes it difficult to connect with the cast when their archetypes shine through more strongly than their own personalities. I quite like the protagonist duo of Rain and Lasswell. Rain is boisterous and doesnât have the gentlemanly qualities of most knights, but is an innately talented warrior. Lasswell, meanwhile, picks up the slack to ensure his adopted brother Rain can rise in the ranks and let his talents shine. But while Lasswell is a more interesting character, he has to give way to Rain, who has unique magical abilities he doesnât understand the origin of. Aside from one major exception, most of your party members are downplayed by the plot past the chapter in which theyâre introduced. Lid is incredibly charming when you first meet her, but past that point her character moments are few and far between. Nicholâs introduction is intense and emotional, but once itâs over, it feels swept under the rug. Past that point, theyâre functional party members that give you more options in battle, and rarely more than that. The major defining feature that sets Resonance apart from other FF games is the Vision system. Youâre able to equip a Vision to each party member, and this Vision takes the form of another character from across the Final Fantasy pantheon. Upgrading Visions gives you access to more of their attacks in battle, and you can freely choose between your own characterâs pool of skills or their equipped Visionâs. Keeping a Vision equipped will enable you to level up a characterâs synergy with it, allowing you to equip abilities and skills from that Vision permanently. Itâs like a hot-swappable job system. If you feel one of your characters needs more curative skills, then you can equip them with a White Mage Vision. If you need access to Water and Thunder element attacks, then teaming up with Cloud Strife is a good idea. There are dozens of characters from different FF games available to unlock and equip as Visions â protagonists and final bosses alike â and this acts as the gameâs main hook. Swapping through Visions, increasing synergy across the cast, and building your main party members to be as capable as possible. “There are dozens of characters from different FF games available to unlock and equip as Visions â protagonists and final bosses alike â and this acts as the gameâs main hook” When collecting Visions from the various Sanctums of Light across the land, you complete a quick three-step quiz to see how well you resonate with the Vision youâre summoning, and the questions are worded so obviously that youâll probably understand what the correct answers are without ever playing the game the Vision is from. Itâs obviously an improvement over Brave Exviusâ gacha system, but these moments feel somewhat cheap, evoking nostalgia for better games. It makes sense for a mobile title, but as a premium game it falls flat. Still, Visions do a lot to spice up a battle system that is otherwise tried and tested. Itâs a traditional turn-based affair with a basic attack, each characterâs own skills, and those of your equipped Vision. You also get access to Limit Break abilities, and modifiers that allow you to build LB more quickly. The final piece of the puzzle is summonable spirits, called Espers, that act as a fifth party member for a short time in battle before unleashing a final strike on your enemies. Otherwise, youâll be using familiar Final Fantasy strategies such as using Protect and Haste to strengthen your team while staggering and damaging foes. Itâs impossible to get lost in Resonance thanks to a map which constantly shows where your next main objective is, along with any side quests youâve picked up. Side quests can offer decent rewards â including some nice upgrades for Lidâs Mecha Chocobo â but by and large theyâre pretty dull, often having you backtrack a bit through an earlier dungeon to witness a new scene or collect an item. Resonance successfully evokes the vibes and atmosphere of Final Fantasy, sure, but it doesnât live up to its inspirations. The battle system and Visions are the standout features, and even they arenât any kind of revolutionary, being broadly bettered by other HD-2D titles from Square Enix . Many of the minor qualms and complaints arenât because of any lack of talent on the behalf of the developers, I think theyâve done a great job adapting a mobile game into a premium title. But the design of its mobile origins limits this gameâs ambitions. Resonance, if it were a truly original title, couldâve been a bigger, bolder celebration of Final Fantasyâs history. As it is, it falls short of that. Final Fantasy Resonance is a fun JRPG releasing just when I personally needed a classic turn-based experience, but in a world with HD-2D rele

sources.text: The PC version of board and card game fusion Culdcept BEGINS will launch via Steam on October 28, Neos announced . Culdcept BEGINS first launched for Switch 2 and Switch on July 16. Total shipments and digital sales have surpassed 100,000 units. Here is an overview of the game, via Neos: A hidden classic that fuses board and card games, Culdcept features a unique, innovative system that has captivated fans since its debut. Players become Cepters, wielding cards in intense battles where luck and strategy collide. After ten years, a brand-new story begins once again. It is a game where you move across the board, claim territories, and build strategies using cards. Use summons and magic to fight your way to victory. Bavrashka, a continent created by the gods. At its center lies the Royal Cept Academy, an insitute where Cepters are trained to wield the power of stone tablets known as “Culds,” fragments of the Culdcept. Kamur, who transferred to the Cept Academy, has his abilities recognized and is selected for the Royal Cepter Guard Regiment. Amid battles that threaten the continent, the power of a Cepter begins to awaken. This is a board game where victory hangs on a mix of luck and strategy. Experience a more accessible evolution of Culdcept that stays true to the series’ charm.​ Combine all kinds of cards to win through the power of your own tactics.​

stories.title: Frozen Trail finally puts the 'raid' in Arc Raiders
stories.summary: The Fallen Emperor and Arc Frigate have me excited for the game's future.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Frozen Trail finally puts the 'raid' in Arc Raiders
sources.text: The Fallen Emperor and Arc Frigate have me excited for the game's future. Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday. I'm standing on top of a flying fortress hundreds of feet in the air, as around me, 15 or so players wage a losing battle against a swarm of flying robots armed with rockets and lasers. It's utter chaos. We fight further and further into the ship, unlocking platforms, defeating waves of enemies and giant turrets which pop out of the deck to gun down unsuspecting looters. But I think we're done. Time is running short and we've once again stalled at this stage of the puzzle. All that's left now is to try and make it back to ground in one piece and live to attempt another day. This is the Frigate , one of Arc Raiders two new raid-style activities, and it's exactly what the game needed. Rather than content you can complete the day the update comes out, Frozen Trail 's Frigate and Fallen Emperor represent a deeper loot chase, tied into upgrading the new outpost and workbenches to fashion special weapons which fire explosive bullets or incendiary grenades. More than that: they're properly fun . I've raided a lot in Destiny 2, completed its dungeons more times than I can count (including soloing some) and I'm quite impressed with the variety of these endgame challenges, how they demand cooperation from players, but also really tie into the features and loot chase that Frozen Trail added. While the Arc Frigate is a pitched battle blasting endless waves of robots as you try to unlock its cargo hold with a bunch of other raiders, the Fallen Emperor is more of an individual challenge. This series of mostly randomised encounters sees you solving puzzles and painstakingly platforming your way through its labyrinth of hazards and Hydra turrets, which love to pick you off when you're dangling in some precarious position. It's a race to perpetrate a bank heist in the corpse of a colossal robot, and if that doesn't get your juices flowing, I don't know what will. Part of the fun is Frozen Trail's new Grappling Hook item, an easy to craft traversal tool that lets you scale and swing in a much more enjoyable way than the game's existing Snap Hook—I always carry one now, just for ease of exploration. The Fallen Emperor is also smart in terms of loot, designed like a kids' gameshow (did anyone here watch Jungle Run?). Players who want the guaranteed big score at the end are incentivised to rush there, lest another raider beat them, but since there are loot containers between each encounter and concealed in them, other players can filter in and still have a chance at getting rare items and rewards for encounters without making it to the end. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. The same goes for the Arc Frigate—it's not just about who gets there first; these encounters are layered with loot, and often reward exploration as much as pushing for the end goal, especially as the new upgrades require a wide range of materials. Though Frozen Trail has its bugs—my reward pass still isn't fixed—this is such a positive update for the game's direction. If the PvE-mode test is anything to go by, we'll soon be able to play Arc Raiders' endgame events like the Fallen Emperor, Frigate, Matriarch, or Harvester without fear of getting ratted and having our loot stolen while we're trying to fight big arc, work together, and puzzle stuff out. I'm not a player who minds PvP or the way it elevates the tension and excitement of the extraction shooter genre, but I think there's a good case to be made for a PvE-only option when running PvE-centric endgame events, which often require cooperation. It's also uniquely frustrating getting ambushed after successfully completing one. This happened to me after landing a huge loot haul on the Frigate and basically being the only raider to make it out alive—I was riding high, I wasn't cautious, and of course some punk with a Kettle was waiting at extraction. He even said "Hello" before he ratted me. It's a sucky way to end these cool events and it dissuades players from investing in their challenge, so hopefully any eventual PvE mode that does appear will include these. Still, these new raid-style events have me so excited for the future of Arc Raiders. I can't help but fantasize about how fun and rewarding a Destiny 2 length raid in Arc Raiders would be, or something similar to Building 21 or Koschei Complex in DMZ—a dedicated mode with its own timer, challenges, and bosses. I can't wait to see what endgame content Embark cooks up next. Arc Raiders guide : What's hot this week Arc Raiders roadmap : New and improved Arc Raiders best skills : Survive the surface Arc Raiders best weapons : Just don't lose them Arc Raiders Expeditions : Retire your Raider Arc Raiders quests : All the missions and how to beat 'em Sean's first PC games were Full Throttle and Total Annihilation and his taste has stayed much the same since. When not scouring games for secrets or bashing his head against puzzles, you'll find him revisiting old Total War campaigns, agonizing over his Destiny 2 fit, or still trying to finish the Horus Heresy. Sean has also written for EDGE, Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, EGMNOW, and Inverse. sources.title: Arc Raiders player numbers hit a six-month high following the release of the extraction shooter's huge Frozen Trails update
sources.text: Arc Raiders is still going strong almost a year after finding viral success, and it's all thanks to Embark Studios' one-two-punch strategy of launching a huge new update, Frozen Trails, to coincide with a free weekend. Arc Raiders' Frozen Trails update upgraded the extraction shooter to version 2.0 earlier this month - 8th October - and quickly led to a surge in Steam players interested in its tense PvEvP shootouts. A new report from Alinea Analytics ' Rhys Elliott now claims a similar resurgence took place across all platforms where the game's available. According to the report, Arc Raiders' comeback peaked with a whopping 1.7m daily players jumping in on the 14th of October, its biggest player count in six months, mostly driven by the aforementioned update. What's perhaps most interesting is that player numbers actually peaked just after the game's free trial weekend ended on 12th October - though around 150,000 new looters reportedly joined the robo-infested wasteland during that weekend period. Both events coincided with the game's steepest discount yet, slashing its price tag by 50% to $19.99. In the three days after the free trial, Arc Raiders sold another 150,000 copies and brought home roughly $3m, not counting microtransactions, per the report. Embark Studios' seemingly went all out this month. Frozen Trails itself nudged almost every corner of the game, adding a new map, new weapons, new menacing mechs and much more. A PvE test also tried to accommodate the game's surprisingly friendly community between the 13th and 20th of October. Executive producer Aleksander Grøndal recently said the team isn't against the idea of permanently splitting Arc Raiders' PvEvP gameplay into PvE and PvP pockets . Who knows? Doing so could open the door to another resurgence if done well. Earlier this month, we learned the production company behind this summer's big screen horror hit, Backrooms, is working to adapt both Arc Raiders and The Finals into film and TV projects . Developer Embark is involved, too.

sources.title: 8 melhores jogos de Star Wars que deixam você ser um Jedi
sources.text: Temos certeza que praticamente todos os fãs de Star Wars já sonharam com a possibilidade de empunhar um sabre de luz um dia. Enquanto na vida real temos que nos contentar com meras réplicas, no mundo dos games podemos tornar o sonho de virar um Jedi em realidade. Há muitos jogos que nos permitem reviver eventos famosos da saga de George Lucas, enquanto outros nos trazem histórias e personagens totalmente inéditos. Por isso, nós reunimos os 8 melhores jogos de Star Wars que deixam você ser um Jedi , seja lutando no chão com seu sabre ou pilotando um X-Wing pelos ares. Confira! Sabemos que há inúmeros jogos que realizam essa fantasia, então tentamos selecionar uma lista mais diversa e apenas com jogos de qualidade inspirados na franquia. Lançado em 2019 pela Respawn Entertainment, em Fallen Order , você controla Cal Kestis, um jovem Padawan que sobreviveu à Ordem 66 e vive escondido , trabalhando em um ferro-velho. Quando sua identidade é exposta, ele precisa fugir do Império e continuar seu treinamento. O combate é um dos grandes destaques, já que exige paciência e leitura do adversário. É claro que também há os poderes da Força, como empurrar e frear inimigos , para complementar o arsenal. Tudo ajuda a te fazer você se sentir como um Jedi em formação. Star Wars Jedi: Survivor , lançado em 2023, se passa mais ou menos 5 anos depois e mostra um Cal mais experiente, mas também mais sobrecarregado pelas consequências de suas escolhas. A história ganha um tom mais sombrio e maduro, e o mundo é maior, com destaque para o planeta Koboh. Survivor melhora o sistema de combate com várias posturas de sabre, entre elas a de sabre duplo, sabre cruzado e a combinada com blaster . Cada uma muda o ritmo das lutas e abre espaço para estilos diferentes. É um dos jogos mais completos já feitos sobre a vida de um Jedi e para muitos fãs é um dos melhores exemplos atuais do gênero. Lançado em 2011 pela BioWare, The Old Republic é um MMORPG que se passa milhares de anos antes dos filmes , numa época em que a República e o Império Sith disputam a galáxia. O jogo permite criar seu próprio personagem e escolher entre classes de Jedi ou de Sith. O grande diferencial é a ênfase na narrativa. Cada classe tem uma história própria, com diálogos dublados e decisões que afetam o desenrolar dos acontecimentos. Além disso, é possível jogar com outras pessoas em missões cooperativas, enfrentar chefes e explorar planetas lendários. Lançado em 2003 pela Raven Software, Jedi Academy é um dos favoritos dos fãs até hoje . Você controla um aluno e o treina na academia de Luke Skywalker, aprendendo o caminho da Força sob a orientação de Kyle Katarn. O jogo se destaca pela liberdade de personalização. Você escolhe o formato do sabre, a sia cor e entre os estilos de luta que o jogo oferece. O sistema de poderes ainda permite combinar habilidades do lado do bem e do lado sombrio . Fora isso, há o modo multiplayer que ainda conta com uma comunidade ativa com vários mods e servidores. Este Battlefront II , da Pandemic Studios, não é focado em ser um Jedi logo de início, mas oferece momentos memoráveis para quem gosta da saga. Após alguns tiroteios mais normais, você pode participar das grandes batalhas no papel de personagens como Luke Skywalker , Obi-Wan Kenobi, Yoda, Mace Windu e Darth Vader. O ponto alto é a campanha, que acompanha a ascensão do Império a partir da perspectiva da 501ª Legião , e o modo Conquista Galáctica, que combina estratégia e ação. Ver um Jedi cruzando o campo de batalha, desviando de rajadas e derrubando adversários com a Força é algo que o jogo fez com mais charme do que muitos títulos posteriores. Merece a lista pela diversão e pelo valor nostálgico. Lançado em 2008, The Force Unleashed apresenta Starkiller, o aprendiz secreto de Darth Vader . A trama se passa entre os Episódios III e IV e mostra o que aconteceu enquanto o Império caçava os últimos Jedi. Nesse jogo, dá para fazer muita coisa, já que você pode arremessar inimigos para longe, destruir estruturas, levantar caças TIE do chão e disparar raios com uma intensidade quase absurda . Na época, o motor de física permitia que objetos e inimigos reagissem de forma realista a seus golpes, o que tornava os combates muito mais dinâmicos. Sabemos que geralmente os Jedi estão lutando diretamente com seus sabres, mas não dá para negar que eles também possuem habilidades incríveis em combates áereos . Esse título de GameCube é ainda mais incrível que o seu antecessor, do N64, e te coloca para reviver algumas das batalhas mais importantes contra o império. Para quem quer algo diferente dos jogos usuais de Jedi , esse é um dos melhores da lista. Além disso, é um dos títulos que melhor recriou diversas batalhas e situações icônicas dos filmes. Lançado em 2003 pela BioWare, Knights of the Old Republic costuma ser um dos mais citados quando se fala de jogos de Star Wars. A história se passa cerca de quatro mil anos antes dos filmes e coloca você como um soldado que descobre ter sensibilidade à Força e se torna um Jedi em meio a uma guerra contra os Sith. O sistema de combate pode ser meio datado hoje em dia, mas o resto vale muito a pena. A trama e os personagens são incríveis, sendo que as escolhas de diálogo e das suas ações empurram o personagem para o lado do bem ou para o sombrio. Apesar da idade, continua sendo uma das melhores formas de viver a jornada de um Jedi. Gostou de conhecer alguns dos melhores jogos de Star Wars que deixam você ser um Jedi? Deixe seu comentário nos dizendo qual é o seu favorito! sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: Tales of Eternia Remastered se beneficia da generosidade do tempo
sources.text: Não são muitas as desenvolvedoras que olham para o passado de suas franquias para tornar seus jogos clássicos acessíveis a novos públicos. A grande maioria se concentra em produzir games novos e ponto. Uma pena para quem, assim como este redator que vos escreve, joga videogame desde os tempos das TVs de tubo. Já faz um tempo que a Bandai Namco, uma exceção à regra, vem fazendo a boa e revivendo títulos consagrados da série Tales of. A empresa japonesa tem se empenhado tanto que relança até mesmo jogos que nem precisavam de um remaster, ao menos não neste momento, vide Tales of Berseria. O relançamento da vez é Tales of Eternia, uma joia dos tempos de ouro dos RPGs japoneses, disponível originalmente para o PlayStation 1 e agora renovado para atrair uma nova leva de jogadores, especialmente aqueles que não tiveram a oportunidade de aproveitá-lo na infância. Quem é das antigas sabe: Tales of Eternia é um produto de sua época e representa bem um modelo de level design dos anos 1990. Trata-se de um RPG tradicional, no qual exploramos um mapa-múndi que conecta cidades, vilarejos e outras localidades, representadas em escala reduzida, tal como uma maquete de escola. Em termos de estrutura, digamos que era o tipo de mundo explorável que o hardware permitia construir na geração dos 32 bits. Guardadas as devidas proporções, era o que eu entendia como mundo aberto nos anos 1990. Ambicioso em escopo, Tales of Eternia veio em uma época em que Final Fantasy e Dragon Quest ditavam tendências que até hoje são usadas na indústria. Lembro que tinha um disco pirata (obviamente) e cheguei a jogar o início de Tales of Eternia, embora ainda fosse muito novo para entender suas mecânicas. Além disso, é um RPG que pode ser implacável, exigindo cuidado na formação de grupos, no posicionamento nas arenas e familiaridade com combos. O que realmente me atraiu na barraquinha que vendia discos do lado de casa foi a arte lindíssima da capa, assinada por Mutsumi Inomata, uma das grandes responsáveis por moldar a identidade artística da franquia. Arrisco dizer que é uma das artes mais marcantes dos RPGs japoneses, com aquele toque charmoso de anime dos anos 1990. À época, Tales of Eternia tentou fugir do óbvio, isto é, da temática medieval explorada à exaustão, e seguiu por um caminho mais Star Ocean, em especial The Second Story, também lançado no primeiro PlayStation. A semelhança está na maneira como elementos de ficção científica são incorporados a uma trama cujo chamariz é o relacionamento entre os protagonistas. Em Eternia, acompanhamos os amigos de infância Reid e Farah, que presenciam a queda de uma nave em seu vilarejo. Após o acidente, eles encontram uma garota vinda de outro mundo, que se comunica por meio de um idioma até então desconhecido, e partem juntos em uma jornada por Infernia e Celestia, dois reinos distintos e opostos. O tom de mistério que envolve a narrativa e o desenvolvimento das relações entre os personagens ainda são aspectos que se sobressaem, mesmo sendo um jogo de PlayStation 1. Confesso que eu havia me esquecido de como Tales of sempre prezou, desde os primórdios, por conexões profundas entre seus heróis, que vão muito além de figuras meramente funcionais. O combate, por sua vez, acontece em tempo real e carrega a marca registrada de Tales of. Dá para ver que o game tenta se distanciar dos RPGs mais convencionais de sua época, isto é, dos jogos por turnos, mas sem abrir mão de ações mais calculadas. Em termos de ritmo, Eternia já flertava com o hack and slash e ensaiava o que viria a se tornar uma característica presente em alguns dos títulos subsequentes. Remasters servem para nos lembrar de que games de qualidade acima da média são atemporais. As lutas em visão lateral de Tales of Eternia, por exemplo, são imunes ao tempo. Encaixar combos nos inimigos é uma gostosura que só, ainda mais com o quê de estratégia na hora de gerenciar os especiais. Conforme mencionei, a dificuldade de Eternia é maior do que estamos acostumados a ver em RPGs atuais, especialmente por conta da falta de balanceamento no combate. Se não tomar o devido cuidado e estiver em um nível baixo demais, você pode ser abatido com pouquíssimos golpes. Sim, farmar faz parte do ciclo de progressão para conseguir avançar na história. A Bandai Namco reconhece que existe um pico de dificuldade acima do normal e, por isso, adiciona os tais facilitadores. São recursos bem-vindos, a meu ver, que dinamizam a jogatina e tornam a experiência mais convidativa para quem não tem bagagem com esse tipo de game. Você pode, por exemplo, acelerar a movimentação do personagem, aumentar o ganho de XP, de dinheiro e até calibrar a quantidade de dano causado, além de recorrer a um seletor de dificuldade. O mais importante é ter opções para adaptar o jogo ao seu gosto e, sobretudo, ao seu tempo. Por trazer o termo remaster no nome, é natural que existam melhorias gráficas e de desempenho. Elas estão aqui, mas são pontuais. A estética pixelada, com personagens 2D e cenários pré-renderizados, envelheceu bem e quase não precisou ser lapidada. Houve um salto na resolução, como é de praxe nesse tipo de relançamento, e os ambientes ficaram mais limpos, mas coisa mínima. Inclusive, você pode alternar entre o visual antigo e o novo a qualquer momento para tirar suas próprias conclusões. A excelente trilha sonora, vale destacar, também ganhou tratamento especial, com melhorias na qualidade da mixagem e tudo. Tales of Eternia Remastered continua sendo um RPG emblemático da era de ouro do gênero. Os anos passaram, mas seus personagens marcantes e sua atmosfera, que transita entre uma aventura aconchegante e uma narrativa com ambições cósmicas, permaneceram à prova do tempo. Se tivesse legendas em português, seria uma recomendação fácil como primeiro contato para quem não conhece a série Tales of. Afinal, sua essência está resumida aqui.
